zh: 『当然，当然，非住你那里不可的，不然就不方便了。』古应春觉得他话中有话，却无从猜测；不过由左宗棠出巡到上海，却想到了好些事。『湘阴到上海，我们该怎么预备？』『喔，这件事我早想到了，因为老太太生日，没有工夫谈。』胡雪岩答说∶『湘阴两样毛病，你晓得的，一样是好虚面子，一样是总想打倒李二先生。所以我在想，先打听打听李二先生当年以两江总督的身分到上海，是啥场面？这一回湘阴去了，场面盖过李二先生，他就高兴了。』『我记得李二先生是同治四年放江督的，十几年的工夫，情形不大同了。当年的「常胜军」，算是他的部下，当然要请他去看操；现在各国有兵舰派在上海，是人家自己的事，不见得会请他上船去看。』『提起这一层，我倒想到了。兵舰上可以放礼炮；等他坐船到高昌庙的时候，黄浦江里十几条外国兵舰一齐放礼炮，远到昆山、松江都听得到，湘阴这个面子就足了。』『这倒可以办得到，外国人这种空头人情是肯做的。不过，俄国兵舰，恐怕不肯。』这是顾虑到伊犁事件中，左宗棠对俄国采取敌对态度之故。但胡雪岩以为事过境迁，俄国兵舰的指挥官，不见得还会记着这段旧怨。
en: “Of course, of course. She must stay with you. It would be inconvenient otherwise.” Gu felt that there was more behind Hu’s words, but could not guess what it was. The thought of Zuo Zongtang’s inspection visit to Shanghai, however, brought several other matters to mind. “What preparations should we make for Xiangyin’s arrival?” “Ah, I thought of that some time ago, but Mother’s birthday left no opportunity to discuss it. You know his two weaknesses: he loves outward marks of prestige, and he is always intent on bringing down Second Master Li. I thought we should first find out what sort of reception Li had when he came to Shanghai as Governor-General of Liangjiang. If we give Xiangyin a grander reception, he will be pleased.” “I remember that Li was appointed in the fourth year of Tongzhi. That was more than ten years ago, and things have changed. The Ever-Victorious Army was under his command, so naturally he was invited to review it. The foreign warships now stationed at Shanghai are there for their own countries’ purposes. They may not invite him aboard for an inspection.” “That reminds me of something. Warships can fire salutes. When his vessel reaches Gaochangmiao, let a dozen or more foreign warships on the Huangpu fire together. The sound will carry as far as Kunshan and Songjiang. That should give Xiangyin all the prestige he wants.” “It can be arranged. Foreigners are quite willing to confer that sort of empty honor. The Russian ships, however, may refuse.” Gu was thinking of Zuo’s hostile attitude toward Russia during the Ili affair. Hu thought circumstances had changed and the Russian commanders might no longer bear that old grudge.

zh: 『应春，这件事你要早点去办，都要讲好，俄国人那里，可以转托人去疏通；俄国同德国不是蛮接近的吗？』『好。我会去找路子。』『我想，来得及的话，罗四姐跟你一起去，倒也蛮好。胡雪岩说了这一句，眼尖瞥见瑞香留心在听，便招招手将她唤了过来，有话问她。『瑞香，』他说∶『太太要到上海去看七姑奶奶，你要跟了去。』
en: “Yingchun, arrange it early and settle everything beforehand. Someone else might help smooth the way with the Russians. Are Russia and Germany not rather close?” “Very well. I shall look for a way.” “If there is time, it would be quite good for Sister Luo to travel with you.” As he said this, Hu noticed Ruixiang listening closely. He beckoned her over. “Ruixiang, Madam is going to Shanghai to see the Seventh Lady. You are to go with her.”

zh: 『是。』『我再问你一句话，太太有这个意思，想叫你留在上海，帮七姑奶奶管家，你愿意不愿意。』『要说管家，我不敢当。七姑奶奶原有管家的。』『那末，照应七姑奶奶的病呢？』『这，当然是应该的。』瑞香答说∶『只要老爷、太太交代，我当然伺候。』『伺候不敢当。』古应春插进来说∶『不过她病在床上，没有个人跟她谈得来的，心里难免闷气，病也不容易好了。我先谢谢你。』说着，站了起来。『不敢当，不敢当。』瑞香想按他的肩，不让他起立，手伸了出去，才想到要避嫌疑，顿时脸一红往后退了两步，把头低着。『好！这就算说定规了。』胡雪岩一语双关地说∶『应春，你放心到湖州去吧！』
en: “Yes, Master.” “There is something else I want to ask. Madam is thinking of leaving you in Shanghai to help the Seventh Lady manage the house. Would you be willing?” “I would not presume to manage the house. The Seventh Lady already has someone to do that.” “Then what about caring for her during her illness?” “That would certainly be my duty. If you and Madam instruct me, of course I shall attend to her.” “We could hardly ask you to serve us,” Gu interposed. “But she lies ill in bed without anyone she can really talk to. She is bound to feel depressed, and that makes recovery more difficult. Let me thank you in advance.” He rose. “Please do not, please do not!” Ruixiang reached out to press his shoulder and keep him seated. Only after extending her hand did she remember that she must avoid any appearance of impropriety. Blushing, she stepped back twice and lowered her head. “Good! Then that is settled,” Hu said with a double meaning. “Yingchun, you can go to Huzhou with an easy mind.”

zh: 胡家自己有十二条船，最好的两条官船，一大一小；古应春一行只得四个人，坐了小的那一条，由小火轮拖带，当天便到了湖州以北的南浔。这个位于太湖南岸的市镇，为东南财赋之区的精华所聚，名气不大，而富庶过于有名的江西景德镇、广东佛山镇，就因为这里出全中国最好的『七里丝』。古应春对南浔并不陌生，随同胡雪岩来过一回，自己来过两回，这一次是一年之中，再度重临，不过去年是红叶乌桕的深秋，今年是草长莺飞的暮春。船是停在西市梢，踏上石埠头，一条青石板铺的『纤路』，却有一条很宽的死巷子，去到尽头才看到左首有两扇黑油铜环，很气派的大门，门楣上嵌着一方水磨砖嵌字的匾额，篆书四字∶『莲池精舍』。
en: The Hu household owned twelve boats. The best were two official-style vessels, one large and one small. Gu’s party numbered only four, so they took the smaller, towed by a little steam launch, and reached Nanxun, north of Huzhou, that same day. This town on the southern shore of Lake Tai concentrated the wealth of the prosperous southeast. Less famous than Jingdezhen in Jiangxi or Foshan in Guangdong, it was richer than either, for it produced the finest silk in China, known as Qili silk. Gu knew Nanxun well enough. He had come once with Hu and twice on his own. This was his second visit within a year, but last time it had been late autumn, with red leaves on the tallow trees; now it was late spring, with grass growing high and orioles on the wing. They moored at the far end of the western market. From the stone landing, a towpath paved with blue stone led to a broad blind alley. Only at its end did they see, on the left, an imposing pair of black-lacquered doors with bronze rings. A plaque of polished brick inlaid with lettering above the lintel bore four seal-script characters: Lotus Pond Retreat.

zh: 『这里就是了。』古应春向跟着身后的同伴雷桂卿说∶『如果我一个人来，每回都住在这里。』说着，找到门上有个扣环，拉了两下，只听门内琅琅铃响，不久门开；应门的是二十来岁的女子，穿着淡青竹布僧袍，却留着一头披到肩下的长发。雷桂卿在船上就听古应春谈过『莲池精舍』这座家庭，与众不同；他处家庵大多是官宦人家老主人的姬妾，年纪有比『少爷』、『少奶奶』还轻的，老主人下世，既不能下堂求去，又嫌在家拘束，往往由小主人斥资造一座家庵，置百十亩良田，供她长斋礼佛，带发修行。惟独这座莲池精舍的『住持』，原是苏州自立门户的一个名妓，只为先后结过两个已论嫁娶的恩客，一个病故，一个横死，勘透情关，造了这座莲池精舍，奉莲池大师的『净土宗』，忏悔宿业。这法名悟心的住持，在家时，便以豪爽善应酬驰名于十里山塘；出了家，本性难改，有谈得来的男客，一样接待在庵里住，但不能动绮念。倘不知趣，她有王熙凤收拾贾瑞的手段，叫人吃了哑巴亏而无可奈何。
en: “This is the place,” Gu told Lei Guiqing, who followed him. “Whenever I come alone, I stay here.” Finding a pull-ring on the door, he tugged it twice. A bell rang inside, and presently the door opened. The woman who answered was in her twenties. She wore a pale blue-green cotton monastic robe, but her hair hung long below her shoulders. On the boat, Gu had already told Lei how unusual this private Buddhist retreat was. Such foundations were generally established for the concubines of deceased officials or wealthy householders. Some of these women were younger than the heir and his wife. After the old master’s death, they could neither leave the family to make new lives nor endure its restrictions. The new master would often pay to build a private retreat, endow it with roughly a hundred mu of good farmland, and support the woman in a permanent vegetarian life of Buddhist devotion, practiced without shaving her hair. The woman presiding over Lotus Pond Retreat was different. She had once been a famous Suzhou courtesan with an establishment of her own. On two occasions she had become attached to patrons with whom marriage had already been discussed. One died of illness, the other met a violent death. Disillusioned with love, she built Lotus Pond Retreat and followed the Pure Land teaching of Master Lianchi to repent the karmic debts of her former life. Taking the religious name Wuxin, she became its mistress. Even in her worldly days, her generosity and skill in entertaining had been famous throughout Shantang. Religious retirement had not changed her nature. She still received male guests whose company she enjoyed and allowed them to stay at the retreat, but they must entertain no amorous designs. If a man failed to understand, she possessed all Wang Xifeng’s skill in dealing with Jia Rui: she could make him suffer a humiliation he dared neither complain of nor remedy.

zh: 古应春是当她在风尘中时，便曾有一面之缘，第一回到南浔来，听人谈起，特地来访。古应春文雅而风趣，肚子里的『杂货』很多，谈什么都能谈出个名堂来，加以善于体贴，在花丛中是到处受欢迎的客人；到了『方外』，亦复如是，悟心跟他很投缘，第一次作客莲池以后，坚约以后到南浔来，一定要以她这里为居停，不过这一回却有负悟心的好意了。『小玉，』古应春向应门的女子说∶『这位是雷三爷。』『雷三爷请。』小玉一面关门，一面问道∶『古老爷，怎么不先写封信来？』『临时有事才决定到湖州来一趟。』古应春问道∶『你师父呢？那只哈叭狗怎么不见？』悟心有条善解人意的哈叭狗，每回听到古应春的声音——哪怕是脚步声，都会摇着项下的金铃，蹒蹒跚跚地跑来向他摇尾巴大吠；此时声息全无，所以他诧异地问。『师父让黄太太请了去了。』小玉答说∶『大概也快回来了，请到师父的禅房里坐。』悟心的禅房是一座五开间的敞轩，正中铺着佛堂，东首是两间打通的客座，收拾得纤尘不染。小玉肃客落座，随即便有一个十二三岁与小玉般打扮的小姑娘，走来奉茶。
en: Gu had met her once when she was still a courtesan. On his first visit to Nanxun, hearing people speak of her, he had made a special call. Cultivated and witty, with a rich store of miscellaneous knowledge, he could make something interesting of almost any subject. His consideration for others made him welcome wherever women entertained, and he was equally welcome in this retreat from the world. He and Wuxin got on extremely well. After that first visit, she had insisted that whenever he came to Nanxun, he must make her house his lodging. This time, however, he would have to disappoint her. “Xiaoyu,” he said to the woman at the door, “this is Third Master Lei.” “Please come in, Third Master Lei.” As she closed the door, Xiaoyu asked, “Mr Gu, why did you not write ahead?” “The business that brings me to Huzhou arose quite suddenly. Where is your teacher? And where is the little lapdog?” Wuxin had an exceptionally responsive little dog. Whenever it heard Gu’s voice—or even his footsteps—it would come waddling up, the gold bell at its neck jingling, to wag its tail and bark at him. Now there was neither sound nor movement from it, which puzzled him. “Madam Huang has invited my teacher over,” Xiaoyu replied. “She should be back soon. Please sit in her rooms.” Wuxin’s quarters occupied an open pavilion five bays wide, with a Buddhist shrine in the center. The two eastern bays had been joined into a reception room kept spotless. Xiaoyu ceremoniously showed them to their seats. Soon a girl of twelve or thirteen, dressed like Xiaoyu, came to serve tea.

zh: 『是你的师弟？』古应春说，『去年没有见过。』『今年正月里来的。』接着便叫∶『阿文，这位古老爷，这位雷三爷。』阿文腼腼腆腆地叫了人，向小玉说道∶『三师兄，老佛婆说师父今天在黄家，总要吃了斋才回来，她也要回家看孙子去了。』古应春知道这里的情形，所以懂她的意思，老佛婆烧得一手好素菜；这天不在庵里，回头款客的素斋，便无着落，特意提醒小玉。因此，古应春不等小玉开口，先抢着说道∶『我们不在这里吃饭。船菜还多得很，天气热了，不吃坏掉也可惜。喔，还有，这一回我不能住在你们这里，我同雷三爷回船去睡。』『古老爷，』小玉微笑道∶『都等我师父回来了再说。』
en: “Is she a junior fellow disciple of yours?” Gu asked. “I did not see her last year.” “She came in the first month of this year.” Xiaoyu then called to her. “A’wen, this is Mr Gu, and this is Third Master Lei.” A’wen shyly greeted them, then addressed Xiaoyu. “Third Senior, Old Buddha Granny says Teacher will stay at the Huangs’ for the vegetarian meal before coming back. Granny is going home to see her grandson.” Gu knew the arrangements here and understood what she meant. Old Buddha Granny was an excellent vegetarian cook. If she was away, there would be no one to prepare the visitors’ meal. A’wen was tactfully alerting Xiaoyu. Before Xiaoyu could speak, Gu said, “We shall not eat here. There is plenty of food on the boat, and in this warm weather it would be a pity to let it spoil. Oh, and I cannot stay here this time. Third Master Lei and I shall sleep aboard.” Xiaoyu smiled. “Mr Gu, let us wait until my teacher returns before deciding all that.”

zh: 古应春点头，问些庵中近况。不一会阿文来上点心；家庵中的小吃，一向讲究质地，不重形式，端出来的枣泥方糕，不甚起眼，但上口才知道香甜无比，本以初次作客，打算浅尝即止的雷桂卿忍不住一连吃了三块。吃得一饱，正待告辞，悟心翩然而归，一见便有惊喜之色；等古应春引见了雷桂卿，少不得有一番客套。雷桂卿看她三十五、六年纪，丰神淡雅，但偶尔秋波一转，光如闪电，别有一股摄人的魔力，雷桂卿不由得心旌摇摇。及至悟心与古应春说话时，开出口来，让雷桂卿大感惊异，悟心竟是直呼其名∶『应春！』她问，『你不说二月里会来吗？何以迟到现在？』
en: Gu nodded and asked about recent happenings at the retreat. Soon A’wen brought refreshments. Snacks at such private retreats were valued for their ingredients rather than their appearance. The square date-paste cakes looked unremarkable, but one bite revealed an incomparable fragrance and sweetness. On his first visit, Lei had intended to do no more than taste one politely. Instead he found himself eating three in succession. Satisfied, they were preparing to take their leave when Wuxin returned with graceful steps, surprise and pleasure lighting her face at the sight of them. Gu introduced Lei, and the usual courtesies followed. She looked thirty-five or thirty-six, with a quiet elegance. But an occasional turn of her eyes flashed like lightning with a peculiar, compelling power, and Lei felt his heart stir. When she spoke to Gu, he was astonished: she addressed him directly by his given name. “Yingchun, did you not say you would come in the second month? Why have you left it until now?”

zh: 『原来是想给胡老太太拜寿以前，先来看看你，哪知道一到杭州就脱不了身。』『这话离奇。』悟心说道∶『胡老太太做生日，前后七天，我早就听说了。今天还在七天当中，你怎么倒脱身了呢？』『那是因为有点要紧事要办。』古应春问道∶『有个人，不知道听说过没有？赵宝禄。』『你跟我来打听他，不是问道于盲吗？』『听你这么说，我大概是打听对了。』古应春笑道∶『你们虽然道不同，不过都是名人，不应该不知道。』『我算什么「名人」？应春，你不要瞎说！让雷先生误会我这莲池精舍六根不净。』『不，不！』雷桂卿急忙分辩∶『哪里会误会。』『我是说笑话的，误会我也不怕。雷先生，你不必介意。』悟心转脸问道∶『应春，你打听赵宝禄为点啥？』『我也受人之托。为生意上的事。』
en: “I meant to see you before going to Old Madam Hu’s birthday celebration. But once I reached Hangzhou, I could not get away.” “That is a strange story,” Wuxin replied. “I heard long ago that her birthday festivities would last seven days. Those seven days are not over yet. How have you managed to get away now?” “There is some urgent business to attend to. I wonder whether you have heard of someone: Zhao Baolu.” “Asking me about him is like asking a blind person for directions.” “From the way you say that, I think I have come to the right person.” Gu smiled. “You may follow different paths, but you are both well-known figures. You can hardly be unaware of him.” “What sort of ‘well-known figure’ am I? Do not talk nonsense, Yingchun. You will make Mr Lei think this Lotus Pond Retreat is still full of worldly passions.” “No, no!” Lei hastily protested. “I could never misunderstand it so.” “I am joking. And I should not be afraid even if you did misunderstand. Do not trouble yourself.” Wuxin turned back to Gu. “Why are you inquiring about Zhao Baolu?” “Someone has entrusted me with a matter of business.”

zh: 古应春说∶『这话说来很长，你如果对此人熟悉，跟我谈谈他的为人。』『谈到他的为人，最好不要问我。』接着便向外喊道∶『小玉，小玉！』等把小玉唤了来，她说∶『你倒讲讲，你家婶娘信教的故事。』小玉一时楞住了，不知如何回答；古应春便提了一个头∶『我是想打听打听赵宝禄。』『喔，这个吃教的！「小玉鄙夷不屑地说∶』开口耶稣，闭口耶稣，骗杀人，不偿命。『』骗过你婶娘？『『是啊。说起来丢丑——』看小玉有不愿细谈的模样，古应春很知趣地说∶『丑事不必说了。小玉，我想问你，他是不是放定洋，买了好些丝？』『定洋是有，没有放下来。』『这话是怎么个说法？』『他说，上海洋行里托他买丝，价钱也不错，先付三成定洋，叫人家先打收条，第二天去收款子。』小玉愤愤地说∶『到第二天去了，他说要修教堂，劝人家奉献；软的硬的磨了半天，老实的认了；厉害的说∶没有定洋没有丝，到时候打官司好了。话是这么说，笔据在他手里，还不知道怎么样呢？』
en: “It is a long story,” Gu said. “If you know the man, tell me what he is like.” “On his character, you had better not ask me.” She called outside. “Xiaoyu! Xiaoyu!” When Xiaoyu came, she said, “Tell them about your aunt’s conversion.” Xiaoyu was taken aback and did not know how to begin. Gu supplied an opening. “I am trying to find out about Zhao Baolu.” “Oh, that man who makes a living out of religion!” Xiaoyu said contemptuously. “Jesus this, Jesus that—and he could swindle a person to death without answering for it.” “Did he cheat your aunt?” “Yes. It is shameful to speak of—” Seeing her reluctance to go into details, Gu tactfully said, “There is no need to tell an embarrassing story. What I want to ask is this: has he paid deposits on a large quantity of silk?” “There are deposits, but they were never paid out.” “What do you mean?” “He said a Shanghai foreign firm had commissioned him to buy silk. The price was good, with a thirty-percent deposit. He had people sign receipts first and told them to come for the money next day.” Xiaoyu spoke indignantly. “When they went, he said the church needed repairing and urged them to contribute. After endless coaxing and pressure, the meek ones gave in. The bolder ones said, ‘No deposit, no silk. Let there be a lawsuit when the time comes.’ But he holds the written receipts. Who knows what will happen?”

zh: 『那应该早跟他办交涉啊！夜长梦多，将来都是他的理了。』『古老爷，要伺候「蚕宝宝」啊。』其实，不必她说，古应春便已发觉，话问错了，环绕太湖的农家，三、四月间称为『蚕月』，家家红纸粘门，不相往来，而且有许多禁忌。因为养蚕是件极辛苦的事，一个照料不到，生了『蚕瘟』或者其他疾病，一年衣食就要落空了。所以明知该早办交涉，也只好暂且抛开。
en: “Then they should take it up with him at once. Delay only breeds trouble. Later he will have all the evidence on his side.” “Mr Gu, they have the silkworm babies to look after.” In fact, before she spoke, Gu had already realized that his question was ill judged. Around Lake Tai, the third and fourth months were known as the silkworm months. Every household pasted red paper on its doors, stopped visiting its neighbors, and observed numerous taboos. Raising silkworms was exhausting work. One lapse of attention could bring silkworm plague or another disease and destroy a family’s food and clothing for the whole year. Though they knew they ought to deal with the matter promptly, they could only put it aside for the time being.

zh: 『应春，』悟心问道∶『你问这件事，总有缘故吧？』『当然，我就是为此而来的，他受上海怡和洋行之托，在这里收丝；放出风声去，说到时候怕不能交丝，说不定有场官司好打，闹成「教案」。人家规规矩矩做生意的外国人，不喜欢闹教案，想把定洋收回，利息也不必算了。我就是代怡和来办这件事的。』『难！人家预备闹教案了，存心耍赖，恐怕你弄他不过。』『他不能不讲道理吧？』悟心沉吟了一回说道∶『你先去试试看，谈不拢再说。』看这情形，悟心似乎可以帮得上忙，古应春心便宽了∶向雷桂卿说∶『我们明天一早进城；谈得好最好，如果他不上路，我们回来再商量。』『好！』悟心接口∶『今天老佛婆不在庵里，明天我叫她好好弄几样素菜，请雷先生。』话虽如此，由小玉下厨整治的一顿素斋，亦颇精致入味；加以有自酿的百果酒，色香俱佳，雷桂卿陶然引杯，兴致极好。古应春怕他酒后失态，不让他多喝；匆匆吃完，告辞回船。
en: “Yingchun,” Wuxin asked, “you must have some reason for inquiring into this?” “Of course. It is why I have come. He has been commissioned by Jardine Matheson in Shanghai to buy silk here, but he is spreading word that delivery may not be possible and that there may be a lawsuit—perhaps even a dispute involving the church. Foreign merchants who do honest business do not want such a dispute. They would rather recover their deposits and waive the interest. I have come to deal with it on Jardine Matheson’s behalf.” “It will be difficult. If he is preparing to make it a religious dispute and means to evade his obligations, you may find him too much for you.” “Surely he must listen to reason?” Wuxin considered for a while. “Go and try first. If you cannot reach an agreement, we shall see.” She seemed to have some means of helping, and Gu felt easier. “We shall go into the city first thing tomorrow,” he told Lei. “If the discussion goes well, excellent. If he will not behave reasonably, we shall come back and talk it over.” “Good,” Wuxin said. “Old Buddha Granny is away today. Tomorrow I shall have her prepare some good vegetarian dishes for Mr Lei.” Even so, the vegetarian dinner Xiaoyu prepared was delicate and flavorful. There was also home-brewed mixed-fruit wine, excellent in color and bouquet. Lei drank with contented enjoyment and grew increasingly cheerful. Afraid he might lose his composure in drink, Gu prevented him from having too much, finished the meal quickly, and took his leave to return to the boat.

zh: 到了第二天清晨，正待解缆进城时，只见两乘小轿，在跳板前面停住，轿中出来两个白面书生，仔细看时，才知是悟心跟小玉。由于她们是易装来的，自以不公然招呼为宜，古应春只担心她们穿了内里塞满棉花的靴子，步履维艰，通过晃荡起伏的跳板会出事，所以亲自帮着船案，把住伸到岸上作为扶手之用的竹篙，同时不断警告∶『慢慢走，慢慢走，把稳了！』等她们师徒战战兢兢地上了船，迎入舱中，古应春方始问道∶『你们也要进城？』『对！』悟心流波四转，『这只船真漂亮，坐一回也是福气。小玉，你把纱窗帘拉起来。』船窗有两层窗帘，一层是白色带花纹的外国纱，一层是紫红丝绒，拉起纱帘，舱中仍很明亮，但岸上及别的船却看不清舱中的情形了。
en: Early next morning, just as they were about to cast off for the city, two small sedan chairs stopped before the gangplank. Two pale-faced young scholars stepped out. Only on looking closely did Gu recognize Wuxin and Xiaoyu. Since they had come in disguise, it was best not to greet them openly. Gu’s chief concern was that their boots, stuffed inside with cotton, made walking difficult. Crossing the swaying gangplank might be dangerous. He therefore helped the boatman steady the bamboo pole extended to the bank as a handrail, repeatedly cautioning them, “Slowly, slowly. Keep your footing!” Once teacher and disciple had come aboard with nervous steps and been shown into the cabin, Gu asked, “Are you going into the city too?” “Yes.” Wuxin’s eyes traveled around the cabin. “What a beautiful boat. It is a privilege to have a ride in it. Xiaoyu, draw the gauze curtains.” The windows had two layers of curtains, one of white patterned foreign gauze, the other of purple-red velvet. With the gauze drawn, the cabin remained bright, but people on the bank or in other boats could not see clearly inside.

zh: 于是悟心将那顶帽后缀着一条假辫子的青缎瓜皮帽摘了下来，头晃了两下，原来藏在帽中的长发便都披散下来；然后坐了下来，脱去靴子，轻轻捏着脚趾。这样的行径，不免予人以风流放诞的感觉。古应春不以为奇，而雷桂卿却是初见，心中不免兴起若干绮想。『你知道我进城去做什么？』悟心问说。『我也正要问你这话。』古应春答说∶『看你要到哪里，我叫船老大先送你。』『我哪里也不去，等下，我在船上等你们。』悟心答说∶『你们跟赵宝禄谈妥当了最好，不然，我替你们找个朋友。』原来是特为来帮忙的，雷桂卿愈发觉得悟心不同凡俗，不由得说道∶『悟心师太，你一个出家人，这样子热心，真是难得。』
en: Wuxin removed her blue satin skullcap, with its false queue attached at the back, and shook her head twice. The long hair concealed beneath it fell loose. Then she sat down, took off her boots, and gently massaged her toes. Her behavior had an air of free and unconventional charm. Gu found it unremarkable, but Lei, seeing it for the first time, could not help entertaining romantic thoughts. “Do you know why I am going into the city?” Wuxin asked. “I was just about to ask. Tell me where you want to go, and I shall have the boatman take you there first.” “I am not going anywhere. I shall wait for you aboard. If you settle things with Zhao Baolu, so much the better. If not, I shall find a friend to help you.” So she had come expressly to assist them. Lei admired her all the more as someone out of the ordinary. “Mistress Wuxin, such readiness to help from someone who has left the world is truly rare.”

zh: 『我也不算出家人，就算出了家，人情世故总还是一样的。』『是、是。』雷桂卿合十说道∶『我佛慈悲！』那样子有点滑稽，大家都笑了。说笑过了，古应春问道∶『你要替我找个怎么样的朋友？』『还不一定，看哪个朋友对你们有用，我就去找哪个。』此言一出，不但雷桂卿，连古应春亦不免惊奇，看来悟心交游广阔，而且神通广大，但这份关系是如何来的呢？雷桂卿心里也存着同样的疑问，只是不便出口；悟心却很大方，从他们脸上，看到他们心里，笑笑说道∶『你们一定在奇怪，我又不是湖州人，何以会认识各式各样的人？说穿了，不足为奇，我认识好些太太，都跟我很谈得来，连带也就认识她们的老爷了。』『喔，我倒想起来了。古应春问∶』昨天你就是到黄太太那里去了？『『是啊。』悟心答说∶『这黄老爷或许就能帮你的忙。这黄老爷是——』这黄老爷单然一个毅字，是个候补知县，派了在湖州收竹木税的差使。同治初年曾国藩派遣幼童赴美时，他是随行照料的庶务，在美国住过半年，亦算深通洋务，所以湖州府遇到有跟洋人打交道的事，不管知府还是知县都要找他；在湖州城里亦算是响当当的一个人物。
en: “I can hardly count myself as having left it. And even for those who have, human feelings and the ways of the world remain the same.” “Yes, yes.” Lei pressed his palms together. “The Buddha is merciful!” There was something comical in his manner, and everyone laughed. When the laughter subsided, Gu asked, “What sort of friend will you find for us?” “That depends. I shall find whichever of my friends can be useful to you.” This surprised even Gu, to say nothing of Lei. Wuxin seemed to know people everywhere and possess extraordinary influence. Where had all these connections come from? Lei wondered the same thing but could hardly ask. Wuxin was frank enough. Reading their thoughts in their faces, she smiled. “You must be wondering how someone who does not come from Huzhou knows so many different people here. There is nothing remarkable about it. I know a good many wives, and we get on very well. Through them, I have come to know their husbands.” “Oh, that reminds me,” Gu said. “Yesterday you went to Madam Huang’s, did you not?” “Yes. Her husband may be able to help you. Mr Huang is—” His given name was Yi. An expectant magistrate, he had been assigned to collect taxes on bamboo and timber in Huzhou. When Zeng Guofan sent boys to study in America early in the Tongzhi reign, Huang had accompanied them as the officer responsible for their practical arrangements. He had spent six months in America and was considered well versed in foreign affairs. Whenever dealings with foreigners arose in Huzhou, both the prefect and the county magistrate would turn to him. He was a figure of considerable consequence in the city.
